an epithet of Purañjaya, son of Śaśāda,

 a king of the solar race, and a descendant of Ikṣvāku; {#ikzvAkuvaMSyaH#}
 {#kakudaM nfpARAM kakutsTa ityAhitalakzaRo'BUt#} <ls>R. 6. 71</ls>. [Mythology relates
 that, when in their war with the demons, the gods were often worsted,
 they, headed by Indra, went to the powerful king Purañjaya, and requested
 him to be their friend in battle. The latter consented to do so, provided
 Indra carried him on his shoulders. Indra accordingly assumed the form
 of a bull, and Purañjaya, seated on its hump, completely vanquished the
 demons. Purañjaya is, therefore, called {%Kakutstha%} ‘standing on a hump’].
